clue.text: For a change Andrew gets the Guardian

indicators.note: making a change means altering the order, so the name's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the man's name taken as written

explanation.surface: Andrew varies his reading by picking up the Guardian newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Guardian' reads as the newspaper, but the definition is the lower-case sense, a keeper or custodian.
explanation.definitionFit: A warden is a keeper or custodian, so the word is a synonym of guardian.

clue.text: Observes crew members on duty

blocks.note: second meaning: the divisions of a ship's crew who take turns on duty

explanation.surface: Someone keeps an eye on sailors at their posts.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means looks at closely; the nautical noun names the shifts of sailors on deck duty.

clue.text: Decided sport came first

explanation.surface: A choice was made to put games ahead of everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule on a matter is to give a verdict, so ruled is a synonym of decided.

clue.text: Cockney saying he has the contract

indicators.note: saying points to speech, so the words are spoken aloud in an accent rather than spelt

blocks.note: a Cockney drops the h of he's, and a tender is the bid that wins a contract

explanation.surface: A Londoner boasts that the job is his.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is both the definition and the accent to use: say 'he's tender' without the h and you get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner from the East End, the traditional Cockney district.

clue.text: Colour's a standard political symbol

explanation.surface: A particular shade serves as a well-known emblem of a political movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The red flag is the traditional emblem of socialism and communism, and the title of the Labour Party's anthem.

clue.text: Peers (Liberal and Conservative) ultimately detest fringe party

indicators.note: liberal means free and loose, so the preceding word's letters may be taken freely in a new order
ultimately means at the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Members of the Lords from the two main old parties loathe a minor party.
explanation.walkthrough: Liberal and Conservative look like party labels on the peers; Liberal is the anagram signal. Respect was a small British left-wing party, founded in 2004.
explanation.definitionFit: Respect was a minor left-wing political party in Britain, the kind of group on the political fringe.

clue.text: In Ecuador, I could see classical style of architecture

indicators.note: in tells the solver the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: A traveller in South America spots buildings in an ancient Greek style.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is the oldest and plainest of the Greek orders of columns, a classical architectural style.

clue.text: Heavy industry in North America

blocks.note: first meaning: moving clumsily and ponderously
second meaning: the felling and preparing of timber, as Americans call it

explanation.surface: It looks like a description of North America's manufacturing sector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy industry' reads as one phrase; split it, and heavy is an adjective on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbering describes a slow ponderous gait, and in American English lumber is timber, so lumbering is logging.

clue.text: German woman's name

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for German
the possessive ending taken as written

explanation.surface: A query about what a German woman is called.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladys is a female first name, so it is an example of a name.

clue.text: West Coast city first to produce excellent computer

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

blocks.note: Los Angeles, on America's west coast

explanation.surface: A Californian city is the first to make a superb computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable personal computer small enough to rest on one's lap.

clue.text: Alan's and Tim's rough charms

indicators.note: rough means crude or roughed up, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Two men's appeal is unrefined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charms' reads as the men's personal appeal, but it means lucky objects.
explanation.definitionFit: Talismans are objects believed to bring luck or protection, which is what lucky charms are.

clue.text: Alcohol initially banned at dance

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the opening letters of the following words are used

blocks.note: the opening letters of banned and at

explanation.surface: Drink was prohibited from the start at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Chap finally tripped, jumping the barrier

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the closing letters of the following words are used

blocks.note: he means a male, a chap
the closing letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A rider comes a cropper at the last fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letter of each of the three words after it, not just tripped.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge is a row of bushes forming a boundary, and in steeplechasing one of the fences jumped.

clue.text: Yet Archer managed to display perfidy

indicators.note: managed means handled or arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jeffrey Archer, the novelist and peer jailed for perjury, still contrived to show bad faith.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods at Jeffrey Archer, a British novelist and Tory peer jailed for perjury in 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfidy is deceitful betrayal of trust, which is what treachery means.

clue.text: Fail to keep appointment with comedian

blocks.note: first meaning: jilt someone by not turning up to a date
second meaning: a solo comic performing to an audience

explanation.surface: A comic misses a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand someone up is to miss a date with them; a stand-up is a comic who performs alone on stage.

clue.text: Arab child worked for Englishman

indicators.note: worked means shaped or fashioned, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A young Arab was employed by an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: it is a man's name, so it stands for an Englishman only by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Archibald is a traditional British male first name, so it can name an Englishman.

clue.text: Game played in nets

indicators.note: played suggests being toyed with, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A sport that is played using nets.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, a game played across a net.

clue.text: Last two pieces of tuna and sauteed flounders made one sick

indicators.note: the closing pair of letters of the next word are the pieces taken
to flounder is to struggle clumsily, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A fried fish dish with tuna and flounder disagreed with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Flounders looks like the fish on the plate beside the tuna; here it is the verb meaning struggles.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauseated is a past form meaning caused to feel like vomiting, a synonym of made sick.

clue.text: Wounded, runs away frightened

indicators.note: going away means leaving, so that letter departs from the word

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An injured person flees in fear.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one R leaves, the one standing for runs, so scarred loses a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Scared and frightened are plain synonyms, both meaning filled with fear.

clue.text: Hesitates to introduce princess to the Royal Society

blocks.note: standard abbreviation of the scientific academy

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to present a royal to the learned society.
explanation.walkthrough: Introducing the princess to the society puts her name right in front of it. Princess Di is Diana, Princess of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to be indecisive and unable to make up one's mind, so dithers means hesitates.

clue.text: Stabbed the Queen's son first, then jumped

indicators.note: first says this royal piece is placed at the front, ahead of the stabbing word

blocks.note: the son of a queen is a prince, abbreviated P
lunged means thrust with a blade

explanation.surface: An account of a violent attack by a royal who then leapt away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts the prince's letter before the stabbing word, though it comes after it in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge is to dive or leap headlong, so plunged works as a synonym of jumped.

clue.text: Like to be asleep, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals one possible version of the word, a rearranged form

explanation.surface: Someone would enjoy being able to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To please is to choose or wish, as in 'do as you please', the same sense as 'do as you like'.

clue.text: The opposite of quick, ready and determined

blocks.note: quick is the old word for alive, as in 'the quick and the dead'

explanation.surface: The reverse of a fast, prepared and resolute person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quick' wants to mean fast; here it is the old sense, living.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dead set on something is to be firmly resolved upon it, so the phrase means determined.

clue.text: Zoroastrian priest's a king of seer

blocks.note: P is an abbreviation for priest
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An Iranian-origin priest is described as royalty among prophets.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is the R of seer itself: 'king of seer' lifts that R out and sets it before what is left of seer.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsees are the Zoroastrian community of India, descended from Persian refugees, so a Parsee is a Zoroastrian.

clue.text: Letters from/to realist philosopher

indicators.note: the letters are drawn from the following words and rearranged rather than kept in order

explanation.surface: Correspondence between one realist philosopher and another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters from/to' reads as correspondence; the slash lets 'to' join the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek philosopher, pupil of Plato and tutor to Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Article about that place

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece concerning a certain location.
explanation.definitionFit: There is the adverb pointing to a location away from the speaker, which is what that place means.

clue.text: Additional charge is made for this in sex trade

definitions.text: Additional charge is made for this

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: A seedy note that something in prostitution costs more.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is an item over and above the basic service, for which a further payment is charged.

clue.text: Trees cut short

indicators.note: cutting breaks the word up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Woodland is trimmed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' looks like one phrase meaning truncated; split it, and short is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse speech is brief and curt, so the word is a synonym of short in that sense.

clue.text: Dark spirit

blocks.note: first meaning: darkness, as cast by something blocking light

explanation.walkthrough: Dark spirit reads as one sinister being; split it into two meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shade is shadowy dimness, and in literature a shade is the ghost of a dead person.

clue.text: Perhaps Hilary's after simple, affordable HP deal

indicators.note: after says the term piece is placed behind the word for simple, though the clue gives it earlier

blocks.note: Hilary is a term of the Oxford year and of the law courts, so it is an example of a term

explanation.surface: Someone named Hilary wants a straightforward hire purchase arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary looks like a person; it is the spring term at Oxford University and the English law courts. HP is hire purchase, British for buying on instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy terms are generous instalment conditions for paying off a hire purchase, letting buyers spread the cost.

clue.text: Continuing, to a smaller extent, after death

indicators.note: after says the smaller-extent piece is placed behind the death word, though the clue gives it earlier

blocks.note: less means to a lower degree

explanation.surface: An idea of life after death, diminished but going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the smaller-extent word behind the death word.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless means without stopping, going on and on, so it describes something continuing.

clue.text: Raved about Saatchi's fourth commercial

indicators.note: about means around and in disorder, so the letters are turned about
fourth picks out a single letter by its position in the word

explanation.surface: Someone enthused about an advertising agency's latest TV spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Saatchi and Saatchi is a famous British advertising agency, which makes it feel like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An advert is a commercial, the short paid promotion broadcast on television or radio.
